voice: Chatterbox (Resemble AI, MIT), default voice, exaggeration 0.5, cfg 0.45

scenes.feature: The problem: a change in one thread never reaches another crew

voice.text: Thursday afternoon, the architect moves a bathroom wall forty centimetres.
He posts it in the office chat.
But the plumbers are not in that chat.
Saturday morning, they run pipe to a wall that isn't there any more.

scenes.feature: Why it matters: the cost of rework

voice.text: Nobody did anything wrong. And on Monday, someone pays to rip it out.
In one industry survey, construction leaders blamed almost half of all rework on poor communication and project information.
This is Second Eye.
It shows you tomorrow's mistake, before it gets built.

scenes.feature: The superintendent's desk beside the floor plan

voice.text: It reads the group chats that your site already uses, and keeps one shared record of the floor.
What changed, who said it, and which crew has heard.

scenes.feature: Build: messages become sourced operations on one record

voice.text: Every message becomes an update to that record.
And every update keeps the exact message it came from. Here's the architect, in his own words.

scenes.feature: Listen + Compare: crew intent checked, the ghost wall, HOLD reply with source

voice.text: Now the plumber texts his plan for tomorrow.
Second Eye checks it against the record, and draws the problem.
Red is where the plumbers will measure from. Black is where the wall is now.
Forty centimetres apart.
And the plumber gets an answer straight away. Hold. Here's why, and here's who said it.

scenes.feature: Per-crew belief: the floor as Novak Plumbing knows it, Who knows what

voice.text: Why did it happen? Each crew only hears its own threads.
So each crew works from its own version of the building. This is the floor exactly as the plumbers know it.

scenes.feature: Rehearse: tomorrow played forward, priorities before work starts

voice.text: Every evening, Second Eye plays tomorrow forward.
And lists what to settle before work starts. The things you can't undo come first.

scenes.feature: Fix: one-tap correction, amber until confirmed

voice.text: The superintendent sends the fix with one tap.
But sending is not the same as hearing. So it stays amber.

scenes.feature: Confirmation of the exact revision, record rechecked

voice.text: Until the crew confirms this exact revision.
Then the record is checked again, and the warning clears. Every step keeps a receipt.

scenes.feature: Crew asks, answer from the record with sources

voice.text: Crews can simply ask. Can we start the bathroom tomorrow morning?
The answer comes straight from the record, with its sources.

scenes.feature: Learn: unplaceable nickname mapped once, next run resolves it

voice.text: And it learns how your site talks. The drywall crew calls unit two oh four the blue room.
The first time, Second Eye asks instead of guessing.
After one answer, it knows. Next time, same words, no question.

scenes.feature: Measured results from npm run eval

voice.text: We measured it. On our simulated test site, it caught all fifteen labelled problems, with no false alarms.
That's simulated data, not a field trial. And we show the numbers exactly as the system prints them.
One shared record, checked the moment a crew speaks, and again the evening before.
People and software agents read the same record. The language model only reads the messages. Clear rules make the call.

scenes.feature: Brand, promise, where to try it, boundaries

voice.text: Context for the physical world, kept up to date.
Second Eye. See tomorrow's mistake, before it gets built.
